It all depends on the Lodge. It based on their membership, activities, and ultimately their leadership's business sense. Most Lodges try to keep it as low as possible.

The most expensive part is in the beginning. There's a lot degree work which is part of the experience that every mason shares. There's some cost on the Lodge's end for materials and a significant amount of effort. Also, I think it acts as a barrier for those who are serious. Expect $150~300 in about a 3 month period (again this varies Lodge to Lodge). After that it's yearly dues, which can run from $30~100 and are due in November/December. A lot of Lodges will make exceptions for those who can't afford the dues.

If you're serious about joining, a decent Lodge will work with you to meet the fees. If they brush you off, you mostly likely don't want to be part of that Lodge anyway.
